content: If you have used certain other medications within the past month, they may interfere with the effectiveness of this product, potentially leading to pregnancy. Always check the ingredients on the label, even if you have used the product before, as manufacturers may change the formulation. Additionally, products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for different purposes. How to Use: If you are using an over-the-counter product for self-treatment, carefully read all directions on the product packaging before taking the medication. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Take one tablet orally, with or without food, as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. After taking this medication, the timing and flow of your menstrual period may change. Notify your doctor immediately if your period is more than seven days late. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, changes in vaginal bleeding, breast tenderness, or headache. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking levonorgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. While it passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), St. John’s wort, seizure medications (e.g., barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, phenytoin, primidone, topiramate), and certain HIV drugs (e.g., nelfinavir, nevirapine), among others. Overdose: Overdose with this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
